D014-D013_h019.question_both:
I’ve felt “off” for a few years now… maybe three? It’s hard to pin down because it’s not like there was one big crash, more like something slowly faded. I plan these beautiful, emotional weddings, but half the time I just feel… flat. I can cry at a commercial, but when I’m actually with a bride or even at home with my husband, it’s like my feelings are behind glass. I’m going through the motions, smiling, saying the right things, but inside it’s kind of muted.

Around the same time this started, my weight crept up a lot, pretty fast at one point—none of my work dresses fit and I had to buy a whole new wardrobe. That made me even more self‑conscious. I second‑guess everything now, from which florist to recommend to what to cook for dinner. I’ll rewrite an email five times because I’m sure I’m messing something up, or I’ll change timelines at the last minute because I don’t trust my own judgment.

It hasn’t totally stopped me from working, but it makes every decision feel heavier and more exhausting than it should.
D014-D013_h019.question_a:
Honestly, it feels like I’ve been running on low battery for years. I can’t remember the last time I felt genuinely happy or even properly sad—everything’s just kind of flat, like I’m watching my own life on mute. This has been going on at least three years now, pretty much all the time, not just in phases.

At work, I’m constantly second-guessing myself. I plan weddings for a living, so every detail matters, but I’m always convinced I’m messing something up. Even when clients say they’re thrilled, I’m anxious, replaying every decision and wondering if I should’ve done it differently. I used to feel proud after an event; now it’s more like relief mixed with doubt.

In that first year this started, I put on a lot of weight—over ten pounds in about a month or so—without really changing what I eat. I still haven’t lost it. I’m too tired and unmotivated to do much about it anyway.

It’s affecting everything—my work, my marriage, even simple stuff like deciding what to cook. I just feel stuck in this low, dull mood that never really lifts.
D014-D013_h019.question_b:
I’ve always been kind of “low,” I guess, but the last three years it’s like a gray filter over everything. Even when I’m executing a big wedding perfectly, I don’t really feel anything—no excitement, no pride. It’s like I’m watching my own life on mute. My husband says I seem distant; I feel more numb than sad most days.

On top of that, this past year it’s gotten a lot worse. In the last couple of months I’ve put on a lot of weight really quickly—my clothes stopped fitting almost between one wedding season and the next, probably more than 5% of my weight in just a few weeks. I eat without really tasting it, almost on autopilot.

Work used to be where I felt confident, but now every decision feels like it could be a disaster. I’ll spend an hour second-guessing a flower choice and still feel like I got it wrong. I’m constantly anxious that clients will hate everything, even when they’re happy. It’s been going on for years, and it’s really starting to get in the way of my work and my marriage.

I keep replaying little mistakes at work or things I said years ago, like I should’ve known better, like I’m always screwing up. Even small stuff sticks with me. D014-D013_h020.question_a:

I drag myself to work, come home, and eat. A lot. I’m always picking at something—leftovers, snacks—sometimes I’m not even hungry, just trying to fill this weird void. I’ve put on weight, and then I beat myself up for that too.

I’m constantly replaying little mistakes: something I said to a coworker months ago, screwing up the timing on the machine one night. I tell myself I’m useless, that I should be further along in life, not single, not stuck on nights. I do this every day, over and over.

I don’t really remember when this started exactly, but it’s been going on for a few years, like since early high school. I’m not sad all the time nonstop, but it feels like my default setting is just… low. Little things make me tear up way more than they should. Sometimes it’s in class if a teacher calls on me and I mess up, or at home if my parents ask about college and I feel overwhelmed. I’ll blink a lot or pretend I have allergies so people don’t notice.

It’s hard to focus now. I’ll read the same page in a textbook over and over and still not take it in, or zone out halfway through a conversation with friends and then realize I missed everything they said. Even watching a movie, my mind drifts and I end up scrolling on my phone instead.

I constantly feel like I’m behind everyone else—less smart, less interesting, like I don’t measure up. Other seniors are talking about scholarships and big plans, and I just feel small. It’s been affecting my grades, and I’ve stopped raising my hand or trying for things because I assume I’m not good enough.
D014-D013_h021.question_a:
I feel like I’ve been stuck in this low mood for as long as I can remember, at least since freshman year, so a bit over three years now. It’s not like it comes and goes in big waves; it’s just always there in the background, most days, most of the day. I get teary over small things, like a teacher giving feedback or my mom just asking how school was. I’ll suddenly feel my eyes sting and have to look away so people don’t see.

My grades have slipped because I can’t focus. I’ll sit down to read for English and realize I’ve read the same paragraph five times and still don’t know what it said. Even watching a show with my friends, my mind drifts and I lose track of what’s happening. It’s like my brain is always half‑fogged.

I constantly feel “less than” everyone else—like my friends are smarter, more interesting, more capable. Even when I do okay on a test, I tell myself it was a fluke. This has made it harder to keep up with schoolwork, apply to colleges, and even stay social, because I assume I’m not good enough and it won’t change.
D014-D013_h021.question_b:
It’s been rough for a while, probably a little over three years now, but this past year has been way worse, like something “snapped” on top of how I usually feel.

I used to think I was just the quiet, “sad kid,” but lately I cry at random times, even in the bathroom at school, and I can’t always explain why. I feel like everyone else is better than me—smarter, more likable, more together. I compare myself constantly and always come up short, like I’m just fundamentally less than other people.

School has really taken a hit. I stare at the same page in a textbook and realize I haven’t absorbed anything. Even in class, my mind drifts off and I miss entire chunks of what the teacher says. It’s the same with movies or even conversations with friends; I just zone out and then feel stupid for not keeping up.

These feelings have been there most of high school, pretty much nonstop, and they’ve really messed with my grades, my motivation to apply to colleges, and even just hanging out with people. It doesn’t feel like I ever really get a break from it—just stretches where it’s “less bad” and then times like now where it’s really intense.
